title: Learned partner model: next-turn partner affect from conversation history and the agent's turn, versus the online linear identifier

persistence.description: predicted valence = A's valence at t; predicted class = A's emotion at t

constant.description: predicted valence = mean training target valence; predicted class = majority training class

identifier_default.description: regesh.bonding.dyad.RecursiveIdentifier with default settings (theta0 [0, .3, .2, .2], P = 100 I, lambda .98), a fresh instance per test dialogue, run online on the valence sequence (A_t, B_{t+1}) -> A_{t+2}, predicting before each update. This is the current platform method.

identifier_pooled_prior.description: same online identifier warm-started at the pooled least-squares bilinear fit of the training examples with P = 1.0 I and lambda .98, to separate the cold-start problem from the model class

ridge.description: pooled ridge regression on standardized scalar features (13): one valence output and a one-hot class block decoded by argmax

selection.criterion: for each feature set, the (pca_components, l2) pair with the lowest valid MSE of the early-stopped valence head at seed 0; ties go to the stronger penalty and fewer components; the class head shares the selected configuration

for each feature set, the (pca_components, l2) pair with the lowest valid MSE of the early-stopped valence head at seed 0; ties go to the stronger penalty and fewer components; the class head shares the selected configuration

for each feature set, the (pca_components, l2) pair with the lowest valid MSE of the early-stopped valence head at seed 0; ties go to the stronger penalty and fewer components; the class head shares the selected configuration

ridge_embeddings.description: linear comparator on the headline feature set: pooled ridge regression over whitened projected embeddings of the three turns plus the 13 scalar features; pca_components and the penalty are selected jointly by valid MSE of the valence output, the one-hot class block selects its own penalty at the same pca_components

protocol.name: within-item preference accuracy for rank_candidates
protocol.items: test examples whose true next A emotion is non-neutral
protocol.comparison: the model's prediction for the ACTUAL B turn versus for one randomly drawn other B turn of the test set (different example; seed 20261027), with the same history
protocol.rule: correct when sign(pred_actual - pred_other) equals the sign of the true target valence: a positive outcome should favour the actual turn, a negative one the alternative; also reported for positive and negative targets separately and as the raw fraction with pred_actual > pred_other
protocol.candidate_description: candidate B turns carry their own gold valence and act in the scalar feature sets; the 'embeddings' feature set uses text only
models: identifier_default (candidate valence through its per-example parameters)
persistence (control: ignores B, ties count as wrong)
protocol.status: a weak, observational proxy for counterfactual usefulness: the alternative turn was never said in this context, and DailyDialog's speaker B is a human

interpretation: Observational next-turn prediction on scripted human-human dialogues. Differences between models describe predictive accuracy for the partner's next labelled affect given what speaker B actually said; they are not causal effects of an agent's expression, and the preference check is a weak proxy. Intervals are dialogue-level percentile bootstraps.
